evidence: rule-1301-accepted-the-lan-client: baseline line 11 declares rule '1301 accept nameserver' (udp, iniface $lan_iface, dport $port, accept); the effect reads the INPUT packet counters (iptables -v -x -L, field 1 = pkts) and expects rule 1301 to have counted the namespace client's datagram to 53 and the stand-in drop the one to 5353 — exactly what an accept on udp/53 from p8test0 ahead of a drop produces under the params fixture (lan_iface p8test0, port default '53'); failed on the clean node (no rule 1301).

a-lan-client-a-responder-and-a-default-drop: lines 1-2 state the class provides firewall configuration for caching nameservers (a complementary rule over the base firewall's default drop); the action builds only on-node fixtures (netns p8testns, veth p8test0/p8testpeer 10.250.0.0/30, transient UDP responders on 10.250.0.1:53/:5353, an appended drop for udp 53,5353 on p8test0 after rule 1301), mutates declares all of them, and the read-only effect checks their resulting state (peer address, unit states, one drop rule), not the action's output.

the-lan-client-reaches-port-53-only: line 11 accepts udp to $port (53) arriving on $lan_iface (p8test0); the effect sends one UDP datagram from the namespace client to 10.250.0.1:53 and one to :5353 and expects '53 answered' / '5353 no answer' — the accept lets 53 through the stand-in drop while the other port, not covered by the rule, stays dropped; failed on the clean node (both dropped).

purpose covered: Purpose (lines 1-2, 11: one rule letting LAN-interface clients reach the nameserver over UDP 53 above the base firewall's drop) is stated correctly. the-nameserver-rule probes the rule text (-i p8test0 -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT, i.e. interface and port restriction); the reach checks show a real client on the LAN interface getting a UDP answer on 53 through a default drop while 5353 stays dropped, and the counters attribute the pass to rule 1301. The interface restriction is checked on the rule (-i p8test0) rather than with a second client on another interface; the kernel's -i match makes that adequate. Honestly uncovered: a non-default port parameter (one fixture per set, lifted_by ubuntu); the manifest has nothing else (no TCP/53 rule at the baseline, so none is expected). All probes stay on the node.
